items.description: Tenant must maintain the non-structural portions of the Tenant Space and its equipment in good order and condition at its own cost.
items.span_text: During the Term of this Lease, Tenant shall, at Tenant’s sole cost and expense, maintain the non-structural portions of the Tenant Space and Tenant’s equipment therein in good order and condition.

items.description: Tenant must reimburse Landlord's reasonable costs of maintenance, repair or restoration plus a ten percent administrative charge as Additional Rent after Landlord demands it.
items.span_text: any reasonable amounts expended by Landlord in connection therewith, plus an administrative charge of ten percent (10%) of such amounts, shall be reimbursed by Tenant to Landlord as Additional Rent within thirty (30) calendar days after Landlord’s demand therefor.

items.description: Tenant may not make Alterations without Landlord's prior written consent, which cannot be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed.
items.span_text: Tenant shall not make or cause to be made any Alterations to the Tenant Space, the Datacenter, or any other portion of the Building or Property without the prior written consent and approval of Landlord, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed.

items.description: Each Alterations consent request must include a full-size hard copy of the drawings and a full set of drawings on CD.
items.span_text: Each request for Alterations consent must contain one (1) full size hard copy of all drawings together with one (1) full set of drawings on CD.

items.description: Tenant's contractors and others must obtain and show Landlord evidence of reasonably required insurance before entering, within the limits of Exhibit B-1.
items.span_text: all such contractors, laborers, material men and others must obtain (and provide Landlord evidence of) such insurance as Landlord may reasonably require, prior to any such entry

items.description: Tenant must remove its Personal Property and restore areas damaged by its installation or removal, at its own cost, on or before the end of the Term as stated.
items.span_text: Tenant shall at Tenant’s sole cost and expense, promptly remove all of Tenant’s Personal Property, and shall restore those portions of the Building, the Datacenter, and/or the Tenant Space damaged by such removal of (or by the initial installation of) such Tenant’s Personal Property

items.description: If Tenant fails to remove its property, Tenant must reimburse Landlord's removal and restoration costs plus an administrative fee after demand.
items.span_text: Tenant agrees to reimburse Landlord within thirty (30) days of Landlord’s demand therefor, for all of Landlord’s reasonable costs of removal and restoration plus an administrative fee equal to ten percent (10%) of such costs.
items.trigger: If Tenant fails to promptly remove any such Tenant’s Personal Property pursuant to this Section 8.4

items.description: Landlord must cause the Casualty Repair to occur after a Casualty Event, subject to the stated sections.
items.span_text: Landlord shall, subject to the terms of this Section 9.1.1, and Sections 9.1.1.1 and 9.1.1.2, below, cause the Casualty Repair to occur.
items.trigger: If, during the Term of this Lease, any portion of the Building, the Datacenter, or the Tenant Space shall be damaged or destroyed, in whole or in part, by a Casualty Event

items.description: Landlord must give Tenant the Casualty Repair Notice as soon as reasonably practicable after a Casualty Event.
items.span_text: Landlord shall provide the Casualty Repair Notice to Tenant as soon as is reasonably practicable following the Casualty Event.

items.description: Landlord may terminate the Lease by written notice in the Casualty Repair Notice if the estimated repair period exceeds the stated length.
items.span_text: in the event that the Repair Period-Estimated exceeds ninety (90) calendar days, Landlord shall have the right to terminate this Lease by, and effective upon, written notice to Tenant as part of the Casualty Repair Notice.
items.trigger: in the event that the Repair Period-Estimated exceeds ninety (90) calendar days

items.description: Tenant may terminate the Lease by written notice if a Casualty Event damages the Tenant Space or Building as described and the estimated repair period exceeds the stated length.
items.span_text: then Tenant shall have the right to terminate this Lease by, and effective upon, written notice to Landlord if (i) the Repair Period-Estimated exceeds one hundred twenty (120) calendar days
items.trigger: If (a) a Casualty Event causes damage to the Tenant Space, or (b) a Casualty Event causes damage to the Building, such that Tenant is prevented from accessing the Premises or the Tenant Space is unfit for use by Tenant in the ordinary course of Tenant’s business

items.description: Tenant may terminate if the actual repair period exceeds the stated length, giving written notice before the stated day of the Repair Period-Actual.
items.span_text: (ii) the Repair Period-Actual exceeds ninety (90) calendar days (in which case Tenant must provide written notice to Landlord of such termination prior to the one hundredth (100th) calendar day of the Repair Period-Actual).
items.trigger: the Repair Period-Actual exceeds ninety (90) calendar days

items.description: Landlord must refund prepaid Base Rent, less sums Tenant owes, if the Lease is terminated under the casualty termination sections.
items.span_text: Landlord shall refund to Tenant any prepaid Base Rent, less any sum then owing to Landlord by Tenant.
items.trigger: In the event that this Lease is terminated pursuant to Sections 9.1.1.1, 9.1.1.2 or 9.1.1.3, above
